discovery: Optical interfaces to single spins in solids: optically addressed solid-state spin qubits and spin-photon entanglement for quantum networks and sensing

nominees.name: Ronald Hanson
nominees.affiliation: QuTech, Delft University of Technology, Netherlands

motivation: These three physicists turned single spins in solids into optically controllable quantum systems. Wrachtrup's optical detection and coherent control of single nitrogen-vacancy spins in diamond created optically detected magnetic resonance of individual defects. It now underpins nanoscale quantum sensing in physics, chemistry and biology. İmamoğlu established semiconductor quantum dots as quantum-optical platforms. His work includes the single-photon turnstile, cavity quantum electrodynamics with single dots, and all-optical spin preparation and control. Together, these made deterministic spin-photon interfaces a reality. Hanson used such interfaces to entangle distant solid-state spins through photons, demonstrating heralded remote entanglement and the first multi-node quantum network. Together they opened a platform that links fundamental quantum control of single spins and photons with transformative technologies: quantum networks, quantum repeaters and quantum sensors. Their work has inspired a worldwide field spanning diamond, semiconductors and 2D materials.
